title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own manuscript. It is a typed Bourbaki draft ('6 - 42 -', redaction 'n° 392') of exercises for Algèbre commutative, chap. VII (diviseurs). It is filed between handwritten pages on L-functions, presumably because Grothendieck, as a Bourbaki member, received the draft and kept or reused the sheet. The neighbouring pages (determinants and Betti numbers of motives, local duality for R_∞f) are unrelated to it.

Setting, from exercise 1 (not shown):
- A is a Krull (or noetherian integrally closed) domain with fraction field K.
- L is a finite separable extension of K, and B is the integral closure of A in L.
- For two A-lattices M, N of L, χ(M,N) is the 'content' divisor of A: the sum over height-one primes p of A of (length of (N/M)_p, suitably signed) times p.
- χ(a,C) means χ(a,C) for an ideal a of C.
- 'Pseudo-inversible' means invertible after localisation at every height-one prime p of A.

Exercise 2 takes an intermediate ring (an 'order') A ⊂ C ⊂ B with Frac(C) = L. Every nonzero ideal of C is then a lattice.
- (a) χ is additive on products ab when a is pseudo-invertible.
- (b) χ is additive when a and b are 'pseudo-coprime', meaning coprime after localising at each height-one p. The hint is to reduce to A a DVR and use χ(a, a+b) = χ(a∩b, b).
- (c) Hence χ(a,C) is the sum of χ(q_i,C) over the isolated primary components q_i of a.
- (d) χ(q,C) = 0 unless the radical p of q has height 1, in which case χ(q,C) = deg_A(q)·p₀ with p₀ = p∩A.
- (e) a is pseudo-invertible iff χ(a,C) = χ(aB,B).

Exercise 3 introduces the codifferent C* = {x : Tr(xC) ⊂ A} and the different D_{C/A} = C:C*.
- (a) The conductor f = C:B equals B*:C*. This follows from duality: xB ⊂ C ⇔ C* ⊂ x⁻¹B* ⇔ xC* ⊂ B*. Moreover (f)_p C*_p = B*_p, using that B_p is a PID.
- (b) D_{C/A} ⊂ f ∩ D_{B/A}. Proof sketch: if xC* ⊂ C, then since B ⊂ B* ⊂ C* we get xB ⊂ C, and xB* ⊂ xC* ⊂ C ⊂ B.
- (c) C* is pseudo-invertible iff B_p(D_{C/A})_p = f_p (D_{B/A})_p for all height-one p.
- (d) If C* is pseudo-invertible, every fractional ideal a with a:a = C is pseudo-invertible. The tool is (ab)* = a*:b.

In modern terms, 3(c)–(d) are the classical facts about Gorenstein orders: the codifferent (canonical module) is invertible exactly when the order is Gorenstein, and over a Gorenstein order every fractional ideal whose multiplier ring is the order is invertible. The page serves Bourbaki's treatment of divisors, lattices and the different, not the L-function project.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. Spot checks hold: the duality argument for f = B*:C*, the inclusion in 3(b), and the identity (ab)* = a*:b.
Cross-reference numbers are left blank in the draft ('relation ( ) du n° du § 4', 'chap. V, § 1, n° '). This is typical of an unfinished Bourbaki draft, not an error.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki draft of standard commutative-algebra exercises (divisors, the different, conductors of orders) that was later published in Algèbre commutative ch. VII. It is only incidentally filed among Grothendieck's L-function notes, so there is nothing Grothendieck-specific or unpublished here.
transcription_corrections: The heading '6 - 42 - n° 392' is a Bourbaki pagination and redaction number, not Grothendieck's own.
The underlined Gothic-style letters are a, b, q, p (Fraktur in print); the transcription renders them correctly.
The final hint in 3(c) reads '(utiliser a))'.
